summary: Backend-only testing for DaySync API. Created comprehensive pytest suite covering auth (register/login/me with Bearer JWT), categories CRUD with default seeding, schedule/notes/events CRUD, event complete toggle, quicknotes CRUD, multi-user data isolation, and Mongo _id leakage sweep across all list endpoints. All 19/19 tests passed against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.

minor.issue: Always returns {ok: true} even when the resource doesn't exist or belongs to another user. Not a security risk (user_id filter is enforced) but is non-idempotent and hides 404 cases. Consider returning 404 if delete_one matched_count == 0.
No password strength validation (accepts 1-char passwords). Consider min_length on Pydantic model.
No brute-force lockout / rate limiting on login (auth_testing.md playbook recommends 5-fail lockout). Acceptable for MVP but should be tracked.

allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True is technically invalid per CORS spec; browsers will ignore credentials. Not blocking since app uses Bearer tokens, but should be tightened in prod.
FastAPI on_event is deprecated; migrate to lifespan handler.

action_items: (Optional) Return 404 from DELETE endpoints when no document is matched, for proper REST semantics.
(Optional) Add password min_length validation on RegisterInput.
(Optional) Migrate from deprecated @app.on_event to FastAPI lifespan context manager.
(Optional, security) Tighten CORS allow_origins to specific frontend origin(s) before production.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 354-line file — acceptable for MVP scope; consider splitting into routers/auth.py, routers/events.py, etc. as it grows past ~700 lines.

Good: Bearer token auth correctly verifies JWT signature + expiry, user_id is enforced on every collection query (no IDOR), all list/get queries use projection {_id: 0} so Mongo ObjectId never leaks (verified by sweep test).
Good: bcrypt used with proper salt, password_hash excluded from get_current_user projection.
Good: 4 default categories seeded transactionally on register; secondary user fixture confirmed each user receives their own seed (data isolation test passes).
Good: PATCH /events/{id}/complete correctly toggles boolean and returns 404 for unknown id.
seed_data_creation: Tests register fresh users with prefix 'TEST_' and clean up created notes/schedules/events/quicknotes after each test. Two persistent test users exist in daysync_db: test@daysync.it (primary) and TEST_iso_*@daysync.it (per-run isolation user — left in DB but harmless).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend public URL: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL — frontend/.env exposes EXPO_PUBLIC_* per Expo convention). Test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py is reusable as regression suite — run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v. Auth model is Bearer token (Authorization header), no cookies. JWT_SECRET in backend/.env. All endpoints return objects with 'id' field (uuid4), never '_id'. Multi-tenant isolation enforced via user_id filter on every query.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. One initial test failure was due to my test asserting case-preservation on email; backend correctly lowercases emails on register/login (best practice for case-insensitive auth). Test was corrected to assert email.lower(); all 19 tests now pass.
